chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Roy Eldridge playing trumpet on his back
summary: At the Three Deuces, Roy would get high and play lying down, apparently just as well.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: L-a-n-h-a-n. Lanhan. They spelled it wrong there, they put a G in there. You know. But a marvelous teacher. But at this time as I told you I was working at the Three Duces, and was with Roy and it was so exciting there. Roy would get high and lay on his back and play the trumpet. And just anything.
Did he play better that way?

He played just as good. We laugh about that. We were laughing about that in New York. Remember when I used to lay (unintelligible) on the piano, you know. The top of the piano, and he would just lay it down on his back and play.
He didn't play any differently, though.
Oh, no, just as great, you know. Yes. At least we thought so any way. But that was a wonderful era,
